content: Miconazole vaginal administration can increase the levels or effects of artemether/lumefantrine by influencing the metabolism of the hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Caution and monitoring are advised. Conversely, artemether/lumefantrine can decrease the levels or effects of midazolam through the same enzymatic pathway. Close monitoring is recommended. The combination of mifepristone with artemether/lumefantrine may prolong the QTc interval, necessitating therapy modification or close monitoring. Alternative treatments should be considered if available. Mitotane, a strong inducer of CYP3A4, can reduce the levels of artemether/lumefantrine, requiring dosage adjustments and monitoring when co-administered with CYP3A4 substrates. Artemether/lumefantrine can decrease the levels or effects of nelfinavir, while nelfinavir can increase the levels or effects of artemether/lumefantrine via CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are necessary. Similarly, artemether/lumefantrine can reduce the levels or effects of nicardipine, while nifedipine can increase the levels or effects of artemether/lumefantrine through the same pathway. Monitoring is advised. Nilotinib and nilutamide can increase the levels or effects of artemether/lumefantrine by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism, requiring caution and monitoring. Artemether/lumefantrine can decrease the levels or effects of nisoldipine, and both artemether/lumefantrine and ofloxacin can prolong the QTc interval, necessitating close monitoring or therapy modification. The combination of artemether/lumefantrine with olodaterol inhaled, osilodrostat, or osimertinib can prolong the QTc interval, increasing the risk of ventricular arrhythmias. Periodic ECG and electrolyte monitoring are recommended for patients on QTc-prolonging drugs. Oxaliplatin can increase the levels or effects of artemether/lumefantrine, requiring caution and monitoring. Ozanimod and artemether/lumefantrine both prolong the QTc interval, and their additive effects on heart rate necessitate close monitoring or therapy modification. Initiating ozanimod in patients concurrently treated with QT-prolonging drugs should generally be avoided. Similarly, paliperidone and artemether/lumefantrine both increase the QTc interval, requiring close monitoring. Artemether/lumefantrine can increase the levels or effects of paroxetine by affecting CYP2D6 metabolism, and both drugs prolong the QTc interval, necessitating close monitoring. Pasireotide and artemether/lumefantrine also prolong the QTc interval, requiring therapy modification or close monitoring. Artemether/lumefantrine can decrease the levels or effects of pazopanib, while both drugs prolong the QTc interval, necessitating caution and monitoring. Similarly, artemether/lumefantrine can increase the levels or effects of perhexiline and perphenazine via CYP2D6 metabolism, requiring caution and monitoring. Posaconazole and artemether/lumefantrine both prolong the QTc interval, and posaconazole can increase the levels or effects of artemether/lumefantrine via CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitoring is advised. Artemether/lumefantrine can decrease the levels or effects of prednisolone and prednisone, while prednisone can also reduce the levels of artemether/lumefantrine. Caution and monitoring are necessary. Primaquine and artemether/lumefantrine both prolong the QTc interval, requiring caution and monitoring. Artemether/lumefantrine can increase the levels or effects of prochlorperazine, promazine, and promethazine via CYP2D6 metabolism, necessitating caution and monitoring. Artemether/lumefantrine can decrease the levels or effects of quetiapine, and both drugs can increase each other's toxicity via QTc prolongation. Avoid use with QT-prolonging drugs or in patients with risk factors for prolonged QT intervals. Postmarketing cases have reported QT prolongation with overdose in patients with concomitant illness or drugs causing electrolyte imbalance. Artemether/lumefantrine can decrease the levels or effects of quinidine, while both artemether/lumefantrine and quinine prolong the QTc interval, requiring caution and monitoring. Quinupristin/dalfopristin can increase the levels or effects of artemether/lumefantrine via CYP3A4 metabolism, necessitating caution and monitoring. Quizartinib and artemether/lumefantrine both prolong the QTc interval, requiring close monitoring or therapy modification. Ranolazine and artemether/lumefantrine also prolong the QTc interval, necessitating close monitoring. Artemether/lumefantrine can decrease the levels or effects of repaglinide, sildenafil, solifenacin, sunitinib, tacrolimus, tadalafil, temsirolimus, theophylline, and tipranavir via CYP3A4 metabolism. Tipranavir can also reduce the levels of artemether/lumefantrine. Caution and monitoring are advised. Artemether/lumefantrine can increase the levels or effects of tolterodine via CYP2D6 metabolism but decrease its levels via CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitoring is necessary. Topiramate can reduce the levels of artemether/lumefantrine via CYP3A4 metabolism, requiring caution and monitoring. Artemether/lumefantrine can increase the levels or effects of tramadol via CYP2D6 metabolism, necessitating caution and monitoring. It can also decrease the levels or effects of trazodone, triamcinolone acetonide injectable suspension, triazolam, and other drugs via CYP3A4 metabolism, requiring caution and monitoring. Triclabendazole and artemether/lumefantrine both prolong the QTc interval, necessitating caution and monitoring. Artemether/lumefantrine can increase the levels or effects of trifluoperazine and tropisetron via CYP2D6 metabolism, while both drugs prolong the QTc interval, requiring close monitoring. Valbenazine and artemether/lumefantrine both prolong the QTc interval, necessitating caution and monitoring. Artemether/lumefantrine can decrease the levels or effects of vardenafil, venlafaxine, and other drugs via CYP3A4 metabolism, requiring close monitoring. Verapamil can increase the levels or effects of artemether/lumefantrine via CYP3A4 metabolism, necessitating caution and monitoring. Voclosporin and artemether/lumefantrine both prolong the QTc interval, requiring caution and monitoring. Voriconazole and artemether/lumefantrine both prolong the QTc interval, and voriconazole can increase the levels or effects of artemether/lumefantrine via CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitoring is advised. Zafirlukast can increase the levels or effects of artemether/lumefantrine via CYP3A4 metabolism, requiring caution and monitoring. Acetazolamide can decrease the levels or effects of artemether/lumefantrine via CYP3A4 metabolism, but the significance is unknown. Artemether/lumefantrine can decrease the levels or effects of alfentanil, alfuzosin, aliskiren, and other drugs via CYP3A4 metabolism, with unknown significance. Adagrasib and artemether/lumefantrine both prolong the QTc interval, increasing the risk of Torsade de Pointes and other serious arrhythmias. Avoid co-administration or use alternative drugs. If unavoidable, frequent monitoring is recommended.
